inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL cash-flow statement, TTM to 2026-09-30: ShareBasedCompensation 73.4 (FY2025 69.2 - 9M-25 56.9 + 9M-26 61.0) plus cash taxes withheld on net-share settlement 21.5 (FY2025 10.4 - 9M-25 10.4 + 9M-26 21.5; no combined figure is published, so the two lines are summed)
inputs.buyback_note: TTM to 2026-09-30 financing-activity repurchases (FY2025 667.3 - 9M-25 620.8 + 9M-26 839.9). The flat count is funded: EXPD retired 1.1m shares in Q3-2026 and 5.4m in the nine months, which is how SBC dilution is neutralised in practice. Buybacks are value-neutral in this model; the cash is already charged as SBC.
inputs.share_count_basis: Cover-page count 129,110,669 at 2026-10-30 (Q3-2026 10-Q) plus 0.20m dilutive awards (Q3-2026 diluted 130.117m less basic 129.918m) = 129.31m fully diluted; held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (expensing and diluting would double-charge). No non-SBC issuance.
inputs.fy0_note: FY0 is the trailing twelve months to 2026-09-30 (FY2025 less 9M-2025 plus 9M-2026), so the flows end on the same date as the balance sheet used for net cash and the share count. Year 1 is the twelve months to September 2027. Using FY2025 as FY0 with the September-2026 balance sheet would count 9M-2026 cash twice (once as year-1 FCF, once as the shares it already retired). The prior version (2026-09-28) used TTM Jun-2026; every forecast year has therefore moved one quarter later.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-18T21:00:03Z regular close (Wednesday); Yahoo Finance chart API
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. 10-year UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~0.95 = ~9.0% cost of equity; no borrowings, so WACC = cost of equity = 9.0%. Cyclicality is charged through the scenario paths and the 25% bear weight, not through a WACC premium, and the same WACC is used in all three scenarios (risk charged once). UNCHANGED from the 2026-09-28 version: no evidence in the Q3-2026 filing bears on it; a move of more than ~50bp in the 10-year UST would.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (ASC 842; liability $576m at 2026-09-30, cost $146m in FY2025) are charged INSIDE EBITDA as US GAAP operating lease cost, so they stay in the flows and lease liabilities are NOT added to net debt. lease_cost_pct_path is therefore 0. One treatment, applied once.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interest is $2.3m at 2026-09-30 (0.1% of equity) -- immaterial, no deduction.
inputs.tax_note: Cash tax rate anchored to FY2025 taxes paid 265.0 / pre-tax 1,094.1 = 24.2% and the GAAP rate 25.8%. 25.5% used in base -- slightly above cash because the model taxes EBIT ex interest income and EXPD has no structural shelters; FY2023's 35% cash rate was FY2022 timing, not a run-rate. UNCHANGED in this update: TTM Sep-2026 taxes paid of 265.9 are only ~19% of TTM pre-tax income (~1.4bn), but that is instalment timing on sharply rising earnings (the mirror image of FY2023), not a lower rate. A change in the GAAP rate away from 25-26% would move it.
inputs.working_capital_note: AR 3,086 vs AP 1,742, accrued 622 and deferred revenue 450 at 2026-09-30: net operating WC ~2.1% of TTM revenue on the full definition, ~10.1% on AR-less-AP. Growth consumes cash (a forwarder pays carriers before customers pay it), so wc_capture is negative at -4% of the YoY revenue change. UNCHANGED in this update, with a caveat: the TTM actual was heavier -- AR rose 1,085 against payables and accruals up 794 in the nine months, roughly 13% of the TTM revenue increase -- because September is the seasonal receivables peak and higher duty rates inflate pass-through customs advances. The year-1 rise and year-2 fall in revenue make the parameter nearly a wash over the two years. If the FY2026 year-end balance sheet (after Q4 collections) still shows consumption near 10% of the revenue increase, the capture should go to about -8%.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route (dcf-methods routing row: operating company, cyclical). Expeditors is a non-asset freight forwarder and customs broker; its value is the stream of owner FCF on the net-revenue spread, so the standard engine applies. UPDATE of the 2026-09-28 build, same model, triggered by the Q3-2026 10-Q: anchors rolled one quarter to TTM Sep-2026 / the 2026-09-30 balance sheet, and only the year-1 and year-2 drivers re-judged (see reconciliation and unchanged_assumptions). The adaptations file was not needed: USD filer, USD quote, leases inside EBITDA, NCI immaterial, SBC disclosed. Interest income (29.8 TTM) is stripped from the FCF base because net cash 1,092 exceeds the owner-FCF base -- the pile is added once in the bridge. TTM owner FCF of 803 is a cyclical high and is itself held down by a seasonal receivables build: Q3-2026 revenue grew 42% (operating income +55%) on AI-infrastructure airfreight, road freight and warehousing, tariff-driven customs work, and -- new this quarter -- a 52% jump in ocean sell rates as the Middle East conflict and the Strait of Hormuz closure constrained capacity. Management says it cannot predict how long any of this lasts and notes carriers add vessels in 2026-27, which is why the base path has a year-2 normalisation and why the bear weight is above the house default. EBITDA margin path is ADJUSTED (pre-SBC) EBITDA on gross revenue; the engine then charges SBC as its own line. The market capitalisation is ~30x TTM owner FCF, versus a 10-year average adjusted EBITDA margin of ~11.4% and 5.3% revenue CAGR. The price is a regular-session close, not an after-hours print.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: through-cycle revenue: between the 5-year (2.9%, FY2020-25) and 10-year (5.3%, FY2015-25) revenue CAGRs
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is NEGATIVE (-2.4% 5yr) while revenue and EPS CAGRs are positive: EXPD returns more than it earns via buybacks (TTM 886m repurchased vs 803m owner FCF), so book value is not a growth anchor for this company. The 3-year CAGRs on every line are distorted by the FY2021-22 freight-rate super-cycle (revenue 17.1bn in FY2022 vs 9.3bn in FY2023) and are not used.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series used for the FCF CAGRs: FY2020 523.9 (607.4 reported - 73.1 SBC incl. equity taxes - 10.4 interest), FY2022 1,933.6 (2,042.9 - 83.7 - 25.6), FY2025 838.1 (953.4 - 79.6 - 35.7). Owner and reported FCF CAGRs are within 0.5pp of each other: SBC is ~0.7% of revenue and not growing faster than cash flow. Per-share figures compound ~4-5pp faster than the aggregates because the count fell from 170.9m (FY2020) to 130.4m; that is the buyback mechanism, not operating growth, and the model does not credit it. UNCHANGED in the 2026-11-19 update: all CAGRs are on fiscal years and no fiscal year has closed since; they roll when FY2026 is reported.

base.growth_rationale: Year 1 (TTM Sep-27 vs TTM Sep-26 of 13,249) +8%: Q4-2026 holds close to the Q3 level (~4.0bn against 4.1bn) on peak season, AI-infrastructure freight and elevated ocean rates, then calendar 2027 runs at ~3.4-3.5bn a quarter as ocean rates and airfreight yields ease. Year 2 -7%: the ocean-rate spike, tariff-driven brokerage surge and airfreight yields normalise, to ~13.3bn. That normalised level is ~2.6% above where the prior version's path stood at the same date (~1.6% after one quarter of trend growth), for the part of Q3 that was volume rather than rate: containers +7%, new customs brokerage business onboarded. Years 3-10 4.0-4.5% fading to 3% are UNCHANGED: through-cycle gross-revenue growth between the 5yr (2.9%) and 10yr (5.3%) CAGRs.
base.margin_rationale: Adjusted (pre-SBC) EBITDA margin on gross revenue: TTM Sep-2026 11.1% (11.3% before the 25m restructuring charge), Q3-2026 alone 11.6%, FY2025 10.6%, FY2024 11.0%, FY2023 11.5%, 10yr average ~11.4%. Year 1 raised 11.0% -> 11.2% on the Q3 print and a year free of the restructuring charge; held below Q3 because high-value technology road freight and rate pass-through carry lower percentage margins (North America costs +51% on revenue +38%). Year 2 onward UNCHANGED: 10.7% in the normalisation year, 11.0% at maturity as the $50m Global Technology savings (~0.4pp) offset yield normalisation.
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 capex guidance cut from ~$80m to ~$60m in the Q3-2026 10-Q; TTM capex 55.9 = 0.42% of revenue. Year 1 lowered 0.6% -> 0.5% in all scenarios. Years 2-10 UNCHANGED at 0.6%/0.55% (historical 0.4-0.6%); D&A 0.5% UNCHANGED (TTM 0.41%, FY2025 0.51%) -- a second year of capex near 0.4% of revenue would move both. Capex held marginally above D&A at maturity.

scenario_narratives.base: Three tailwinds -- AI-infrastructure freight (air charters, specialised road freight and warehousing for hyperscalers), tariff-driven customs complexity lifting the brokerage line, and since Q2-2026 an ocean-rate spike from Middle East capacity constraints -- hold through the Q4-2026 peak (year 1 +8%), then fade through 2027-28 as new vessels and freighter capacity arrive, tariff work runs off and yields normalise (year 2 -7%). Thereafter gross revenue compounds at the through-cycle 3-4.5%, and the adjusted EBITDA margin settles at 11.0% as the $50m technology restructuring savings offset yield normalisation. Owner FCF margin on gross revenue ~7%, in line with the FY2023-25 average of 7.4%. Terminal value is capped at 17x owner FCF (Gordon at 9%/3% would be 17.2x), consistent with a mature, high-ROIC but rate-cyclical forwarder.
scenario_narratives.bull: AI data-centre hardware becomes a durable, growing freight vertical uncorrelated with retail cycles, so year 1 grows 12% and the rate normalisation costs only 3% in year 2; the tariff regime keeps proliferating (Section 301/232, IEEPA) so customs brokerage -- growing 25-29% in 2026 on new business -- keeps compounding at the highest margin in the mix; CEO Wall's market-share gains persist and the technology restructuring plus AI productivity in customs processing lift the adjusted EBITDA margin to 12% (its FY2016-21 range). Growth 6% in years 3-4 fading to 3.5%; terminal cap 18x.
scenario_narratives.bear: The episodic drivers reverse together from a higher peak: the Strait of Hormuz reopens and new vessels flood ocean capacity, hyperscaler capex digests, freighter capacity catches up and airfreight rates fall (year 1 +3%, year 2 -18%, a FY2023-style unwind landing at ~11.2bn, about where the prior version's bear stood); a US-China de-escalation or accelerated sourcing diversification away from the China/Hong Kong lanes (~19% of revenue) removes the customs surge; a trade slowdown compresses volumes and yields simultaneously. Margin troughs at 9.6% (only marginally above the FY2008-09 ~9%-9.5% GAAP trough, because customs mix is richer now) and recovers only to 10.3%. Cap 15x, terminal growth 2.5%. Bear remains solidly cash-generative -- there is no solvency dimension, only a de-rating.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: UNCHANGED at 25/50/25. Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25% because the FCF base is a cyclical high built on tailwinds management itself says it cannot predict -- now including a geopolitical ocean-rate spike, the most transient kind -- and the price sits in the upper part of its 52-week range. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things to hold at once: durable AI freight demand, a persistently complex tariff regime, and margin expansion to 12%. No solvency risk in any path, so the bear is a de-rating, not an impairment. Two more quarters of AI-related volume growth after ocean rates have normalised would be the evidence for moving weight from bear to bull.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value the through-cycle owner FCF of an asset-light forwarder, not the current print. Revenue and yield are set by freight rates the company does not control, so the model normalises the 2026 AI-freight, tariff-customs and ocean-rate spike in year 2 and capitalises a mature 11% adjusted EBITDA margin at a capped multiple. Buybacks are the mechanism that holds the count flat and are not credited as growth; the net-cash pile is added once and its interest stripped from the flows.
key_risks_to_valuation: Freight-rate cycle: gross revenue swung 17.1bn (FY2022) to 9.3bn (FY2023); Q3-2026 ran at a 16.4bn annualised rate, and the year-2 normalisation could be deeper (bear -18%) or shallower (bull -3%)
Durability of AI-hyperscaler airfreight demand -- a new vertical with no cycle history
US tariff regime: complexity drives the highest-margin customs line up, but volume destruction or a de-escalation drives it down; ~19% of revenue on China/Hong Kong export lanes
Non-asset model has no structural cost advantage versus Kuehne+Nagel, DSV, DHL; digital forwarders and direct carrier relationships are a disintermediation risk
Buybacks at ~30x owner FCF (Q3-2026 average $178.36) transfer value from continuing holders if the intrinsic value here is right
Terminal value is capped (17x) rather than Gordon; a market that keeps paying 25x+ earnings for EXPD will disagree with this model indefinitely

Working capital: the September balance sheet carries a seasonal and duty-advance receivables build; the model's -4% capture is lighter than the TTM actual (~-13%) and is flagged for review at FY2026 year-end
